edits.before: The da Vinci architecture is the pattern the whole field inherited. A surgeon sits at a console away from the table and manipulates hand controllers; a patient-side cart holds three or four articulated arms carrying wristed instruments and an endoscope; a vision stack delivers a magnified stereoscopic view. The machine contributes what a hand holding a laparoscopic stick cannot: motion scaling that divides hand movement into finer instrument movement, tremor filtering, and wrists that articulate inside the body, beyond the wall. The surgeon remains the planner and the controller. In the framework Yang and colleagues proposed for the field, that is Level 0 autonomy, no autonomy, and the framework's authors are explicit that a surgical robot with motion scaling still belongs there because the output represents the surgeon's desired motion <Cite id="yang-autonomy-2017" />.

edits.before: One robust layout for a learned-policy graph separates drivers, state assembly, a policy server, a command gate, a controller bridge and a supervisor. The supervisor can drive ROS 2 managed nodes, which leave a primary state only at an external supervisor's request or on an error in the Active state <Cite id="ros2-lifecycle-design-2015" />. Inference stays outside the hard real-time loop unless its worst case fits; ROS 2's real-time guidance keeps page faults, dynamic allocation and indefinitely blocking synchronization out of that path <Cite id="ros2-realtime-docs-2026" />. Lyrical's EventsCBGExecutor cuts executor CPU overhead, but its event queue is unbounded <Cite id="ros2-executors-2026" />.

Hwangbo and colleagues learned an actuator network for ANYmal's series-elastic actuators. It predicts joint torque from current and past joint-position errors and velocities, trained on data from exciting the real legs and disturbing the robot by hand. It stands in for actuation in the simulator. Policies trained with ideal or analytical actuator models failed to take a single step without falling. A separate recovery policy flipped ANYmal upright from nine tested configurations, including a nearly upside-down pose and two resting on its own legs, after the authors relaxed joint-velocity constraints following the first hardware attempt <Cite id="hwangbo-2019" />.

edits.before: Rudin and colleagues trained flat-terrain walking in under four minutes on one workstation GPU. Their deployment policy used 4,096 ANYmal robots, batches of 98,304 transitions (24 steps per robot) and 1,500 updates in under twenty minutes on an i9-11900k CPU and RTX A6000 GPU. Their game-inspired terrain curriculum promotes robots that cross a tile, demotes those covering under half the commanded distance, and loops hardest-level solvers back to a random level . The released `legged_gym` repository (October 2021) is the Isaac Gym environment used to train ANYmal on rough terrain .

edits.before: <Term id="offline-reinforcement-learning">Offline RL</Term> learns from a static set of transitions `(observation, action, reward, next observation, termination)` produced by one or more behavior policies <Cite id="offline-rl-tutorial-2020" />. Value learning bootstraps, so error from actions outside the data accumulates through the Bellman backup <Cite id="bear-2019" />. For robots, support also spans commanded frame, controller mode, action magnitude, contact regime, task stage and recovery. LWD applies offline-to-online RL to a pretrained VLA across a fleet of 16 dual-arm robots and reports 95% average success over eight tasks <Cite id="lwd-2026" />. Q2RL keeps a behavior-cloning policy's good actions by gating between cloned and RL actions on their Q-values, and learned contact-rich pipe assembly and kitting on a robot in one to two hours <Cite id="q2rl-2026" />. BORA updates only a residual actor on a frozen VLA, raising success on standard objects from 60.8% to 82.5% with 20 online trajectories per task <Cite id="bora-2026" />. The [RL fine-tuning guide](/manipulation/rl-finetuning) covers this phase.

An <Term id="on-policy">on-policy</Term> method's update is valid only for data the current policy generated, so each batch is collected, consumed and discarded. PPO alternates sampling with optimizing a surrogate objective that allows several minibatch epochs per batch, where plain policy gradient takes one step <Cite id="ppo-2017" />. An <Term id="off-policy">off-policy</Term> method improves one policy from data another produced, so experience accumulates in a <Term id="replay-buffer">replay buffer</Term>. Underneath is <Term id="q-learning">Q-learning</Term>: fit the value of a state-action pair and bootstrap from the best next action, even one never taken <Cite id="sutton-barto-2018" />.

Visual Dexterity reorients novel shapes in a median of about seven seconds on hardware under \$5,000 <Cite id="visual-dexterity-2022" />. DextrAH-RGB [transfers](/rl-sim2real/sim2real-transfer/) an end-to-end RGB grasping policy <Cite id="dextrah-rgb-2024" />, distilled from a privileged teacher into a stereo-RGB student for a KUKA arm and Allegro hand <Cite id="isaac-lab-2025" />.
